text:
jen: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — thanks everyone for the writeup. We need owners for the rollout hardening items: auto-rollback hooks, stricter initial blast radius, and a recurring-pattern detector for canary failures. Short thread to assign and set dates.

alex: I can pick up the feature-flag/rollout-side changes. Plan: default rollout is 0.5% for new experiments, require explicit opt-in for >5%. Need to update our flagging library and console UI. :+1:

mike: Re auto-rollback — we should wire a light-weight policy into the router that checks error-rate & latency delta over sliding window and triggers rollback if thresholds crossed. Prototype below:

```
policy: 
  window: 120s
  error_rate_threshold: 0.10
  latency_p90_increase_pct: 40
  action: rollback_to_previous
```

mike: I'll prototype the hook and add tests. Estimated prototype by 2026-04-08.

priya: I'll own telemetry & alerting rules in Console. Need two new signals: canary_error_rate and canary_latency_delta. I'll add dashboards and the evaluators that feed the auto-rollback decision. ETA: 2026-04-05.

sam: Ops-side: we need safe rollbacks for in-flight requests and a clear runbook. I'll draft a short rollback playbook and make the rollback action idempotent. Can have first draft by EOD next Tue.

ops-bot: Incident doc: https://redwood.company/incidents/2026-03-18-canary-regression — linked for context.

jen: Nice. To avoid scope creep, let's make minimal viable changes first: (1) library + default 0.5% blast radius (alex), (2) basic policy + test harness (mike), (3) telemetry + Console signals (priya), (4) rollback runbook (sam). We'll iterate after.

jen: Owners + commitments: alex -> flag defaults & console UX update (PR + rollout plan) by 2026-04-12; mike -> auto-rollback prototype with unit tests by 2026-04-08; priya -> telemetry + alerts + dashboard by 2026-04-05; sam -> rollback runbook + playbook by 2026-04-07.

alex: Can we add a pre-rollout checklist that gates rolling >0.5%? e.g., must have smoke tests green, fingerprint checks, and canary traffic shape validated. I can add the check to the console flow.

priya: Agree. Also recommend a weekly job that scans past 90 days of rollouts and flags recurring patterns by team/model. We saw similar stack traces across two incidents last quarter. Could automate a simple cluster-by-signature. I can add it as a low-priority follow-up (ETA: 2026-04-22).

mike: One more: for memory/kv-cache regressions, consider a canary variant that runs in shadow mode for 10% of traffic concurrently to detect perf regressions without affecting users. That reduces blast radius while catching degradations.

jen: Good idea — mark as backlog item for Optimize team.

sam: Question: how do we ensure rollbacks don't cascade and cause flapping? Suggest a cooldown window after rollback (e.g., 30m) where automated re-rollouts are blocked unless manually approved. I'll add to runbook.

jen: Agreed — cooldown = 30m default. If teams want shorter they need a documented exception.

alex: I'll open the initial PRs tonight for the flag library fix and the console gating stub. Will tag reviewers: @mike @priya.

jen: Thanks — let's reconvene next Fri for status. I'll update the postmortem with these action items and owner list. Short action summary (copyable):

- alex: flag defaults & console gating (0.5% default) — 2026-04-12
- mike: auto-rollback prototype + tests — 2026-04-08
- priya: telemetry signals + dashboards + weekly pattern scan (follow-up) — 2026-04-05 / 2026-04-22
- sam: rollback runbook + cooldown policy — 2026-04-07
- backlog: shadow-mode perf canary (Optimize) — no ETA

jen: If anyone needs help or wants to swap ownership, speak up here. :slightly_smiling_face:

alex: All good from me. I'll cc eng-sre and devex once PRs land.

mike: Will put up a draft test harness in the next 48h.

priya: Starting work tomorrow morning. Will post dashboard links when ready.

sam: Adding runbook to /docs/runbooks/rollback-canary.md and will ping the oncall test channel when it's ready.

jen: Closing loop — thanks team. We'll make this standard for future canaries.
